personal.bio: I'm a Master's student in Electrical and Computer Engineering at UC San Diego, specializing in Machine Learning and Data Science. My work focuses on agentic AI, multi-agent systems, and the full LLM lifecycle—from fine-tuning and alignment to inference optimization and safety. I'm fascinated by how intelligent systems reason, collaborate, and scale, especially at the intersection of modeling, systems design, and real-world impact. I learn by building, questioning assumptions, and experimenting. Whether it's orchestrating LLMs as goal-driven agents or designing guardrails for trustworthy AI, I'm drawn to problems where technical depth meets product thinking. Based in San Diego, I'm always open to research discussions and collaborations that push the boundaries of AI systems.

projects.title: Fashion Recommendation System
projects.description: Designed a four-stage recommendation pipeline that transformed raw H&M transaction data into a production-ready system. The workflow progressed from data preprocessing to multi-strategy candidate generation, feature engineering, and ensemble model training, with each stage building on the last. The system was optimized for memory efficiency and Apple Silicon performance, and evaluated rigorously to ensure strong results on the MAP@12 metric.

projects.title: Time Series Forecasting for Walmart Retail Sales
projects.description: I built retail demand forecasting pipeline on Walmart’s M5 hierarchical sales data, comparing classical time series models with modern machine learning and deep learning approaches. The work focused on practical challenges such as feature engineering from calendar and pricing data, handling seasonality and intermittent demand, and balancing accuracy with computational efficiency. By benchmarking models including ARIMA variants, gradient boosting, and N-BEATS, I derived actionable insights on which approaches scale best for production use, highlighting how model choice and data design directly impact forecasting reliability in real-world retail systems.

projects.title: Meeting Accountability Engine
projects.description: Extracts commitments from meeting transcripts (Zoom VTT), tracks follow-ups, and surfaces renegotiations via Discord. Built a four-stage LLM pipeline with Gemini, Postgres, LEANN vector search, Celery beat jobs, and a React dashboard for CSE291P PA4.

projects.title: Adaptive Draft Length Controller for DFlash Speculative Decoding
projects.description: Built an adaptive DFlash speculative decoding controller that replaces a constant draft block length with LinUCB-selected variable draft lengths. The controller uses the target model's confidence on the last accepted bonus token, plus an EMA-smoothed confidence signal, to choose block-size arms during generation and update the policy from acceptance-efficiency rewards for faster response generation.

projects.title: CRS-SSD: Safety-Aware Speculative Decoding
projects.description: Extended Speculative Safety-Aware Decoding with a per-token Composite Risk Score that replaces coarse binary mode-switching. Best configuration achieved 20.0% ASR on a high-ASR evaluation set with zero over-refusal.

projects.title: Allerion: Pollen Forecast
projects.description: Pollen forecast system that uses iNaturalist data and Google's Pollen API to predict pollen levels for a given location. It uses a combination of machine learning and natural language processing to predict the pollen levels. It also uses a heatmap to visualize the pollen levels.

projects.title: Legacy Architecture Modernization Engine
projects.description: AI-powered tool that analyzes legacy GitHub repositories via the Nia API, generates step-by-step migration plans with an LLM, and executes file changes with git commits and Markdown migration reports.

projects.title: Academic Abstract Monitor
projects.description: Monitors arXiv for ML systems papers, applies optional keyword pre-filtering, and classifies abstracts with a two-stage Gemini pipeline (Flash Lite first pass, Flash escalation). Includes evaluation harness with gold dataset metrics.

projects.title: Document Scanner
projects.description: Upload receipt or bill images, run Tesseract OCR, extract structured fields with dual local Ollama models (Gemma + GLM), fall back to Gemini when confidence is low, and evaluate against ground truth.

projects.title: TermAgent
projects.description: CSE291P Assignment 3 agent project. Includes AgentDev (paper/PRD to runnable Python with Next.js IDE, Docker sandbox, and pass@k evaluation) and bashBuddy terminal agent tooling.

description: I designed and deployed production-grade generative AI systems spanning agentic workflows, retrieval-augmented generation, and enterprise AI platforms on AWS. My work included building multi-agent orchestration, LLMOps monitoring, and safety guardrails, for document intelligence, and CRM-focused AI applications using tools like LangChain, FastAPI, and cloud-native services.

The systems I helped build reduced manual effort and response times at scale, enabling faster decision-making and more reliable AI deployments for enterprise teams. These solutions automated high-volume workflows, improved customer engagement through real-time AI assistance, and delivered secure, observable, and dependable AI systems used daily in production environments.

I built RAG-based systems for entity extraction and long-document summarization, with a focus on processing complex legal texts. This included prompt engineering for structured clause and sub-clause extraction from large contracts, as well as research into OCR-based approaches for reliable clause detection in scanned legal documents.

The solutions significantly improved accuracy and efficiency in legal document analysis, boosting extraction precision. This enabled faster review of large contracts and laid the groundwork for scalable, AI-assisted legal document analysis workflows.

I focused on improving semantic representations for code-mixed customer support dialogues by generating high-quality text embeddings at scale. This involved large-scale text preprocessing, fine-tuning transformer models using unsupervised contrastive learning methods, and pre-training multilingual models with masked language modeling to better capture semantic similarity across noisy, real-world text.

The improved embeddings led to significantly denser and more coherent clusters, enabling better grouping of semantically similar conversations. This directly enhanced downstream analysis and understanding of customer support interactions, improving the reliability of large-scale text clustering in multilingual and code-mixed settings.

I built and scaled an AWS-based Capsule measurement deployment to study cloud network bottlenecks, extending a single-region setup to us-east-1, us-east-2, us-west-1, and us-west-2 with region-specific AMIs, isolated VPCs, and mirrored subnet routing.

I automated the full measurement pipeline with Terraform and Bash orchestration: Capsule and traffic instance deployment, staged bootstrap, public-Ookla route enablement, receiver NAT, multi-region Ookla test execution, and CSV collection to local storage and S3.

I improved measurement reliability by validating DPDK bridge behavior, port-8080 flow capture in Capsule DATA CSVs, configurable Ookla server selection, and deployment/experiment runbooks with observability checks for bootstrap, routing, and result verification.

I explored the use of machine learning to accelerate solution search for the Graph Clear Problem, modeling pursuit–evasion scenarios on 2D planar graphs. This involved formulating the problem using constraint programming, generating synthetic training data, engineering informative graph features, and training decision tree regressors to learn interpretable decision rules.

The learned models achieved comparable solution quality to traditional methods while improving search efficiency for small-scale instances. This work demonstrated how ML-driven heuristics can complement classical optimization techniques by reducing solution time without sacrificing correctness.
